issues.title: Products can be created with a zero or negative price
issues.symptoms: The catalogue team reports products appearing in the store for Rs 0.00 and, in one case, a negative price.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating a product with a price of zero is rejected with a ValidationError.
Creating a product with a negative price is rejected with a ValidationError.
Products with a positive whole-number price are still created as before.
hints: Look at every rule createProduct checks before it saves a product. Which property of a price is never checked?
The price check confirms the value is a whole number, but a whole number can still be zero or below zero.
Extend the price validation in productService.js so that only values greater than zero are accepted.
Add a condition next to Number.isInteger(priceInPaise) that rejects priceInPaise <= 0 by throwing the same ValidationError type.

issues.title: Adding the same product twice resets the cart quantity
issues.symptoms: Customers who add 2 earbuds and then 3 more see only 3 in their cart instead of 5. Support tickets mention carts 'losing' items.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding a product that is already in the cart increases its quantity by the amount added.
Adding a new product still creates a new cart line.
The cart total reflects the combined quantity.
hints: Reproduce it: add the same product to one cart twice and inspect the cart. What happens to the first quantity?
addItem treats an existing line and a new line differently. Read the branch that handles an existing line carefully.
When the product is already in the cart, the new quantity should be combined with the existing one rather than replacing it.
In the existingItem branch of addItem, the assignment overwrites the quantity. Change it so the added quantity is added to existingItem.quantity.

issues.title: Failed checkouts leave inventory counts wrong
issues.symptoms: The warehouse sees stock counts drift lower than reality. It happens after customers try to buy several items and checkout fails because one item is out of stock.
acceptanceCriteria: If any item in the cart does not have enough stock, checkout fails with a ConflictError.
A failed checkout does not change the stock of any product.
A successful checkout still reduces stock for every item and clears the cart.
hints: Put two products in a cart where only the second one is out of stock, then try to check out. Compare stock before and after.
checkout changes stock while it is still deciding whether the order is valid. What happens to the changes already made when it throws halfway?
Separate checking from changing: confirm every item has enough stock first, and only then reduce stock for all of them.
Use two loops in checkout: the first only validates stock and throws a ConflictError if needed, the second performs the product.stock -= item.quantity updates.
